facts.fact: Circulaire n° 16 of 22 July 2024, issued by the Head of Government to ministers, governors and heads of public bodies, generalises public bodies' adoption of cloud computing under the 'TN Government Cloud First Policy', and is listed as in force.
facts.system: TN Government Cloud First Policy (Circulaire n° 16)

facts.fact: The circular sets four hosting tiers: sensitive internal systems go in a private cloud or national or sectoral government cloud centres, shared G2G systems in government cloud centres, and citizen and business e-services in the body's private cloud, government cloud centres or providers holding the N-Cloud label, with G-Cloud labelled providers as the fallback for the first two tiers.

facts.fact: The ministerial order of 13 September 2023 (JORT no. 106, 15 September 2023) requires public bodies' software, platforms and infrastructure to be hosted in-house or with cloud providers according to four tiers, and makes any other arrangement subject to prior ANCS approval.

facts.fact: The order sets the hosting tiers as the body's own private cloud, a G-cloud labelled government provider, an N-cloud labelled national provider, and unlabelled providers, with ANCS issuing the labels, valid one year, to Tunisian providers with data centres on Tunisian territory.

facts.fact: The National Cybersecurity Agency's register of labelled cloud providers, version 3.3 of 20 November 2025, lists seven N-Cloud labelled providers, each with a one-year validity, and no G-Cloud label.

Tunisia's communications technologies ministry said the G-Cloud and N-Cloud labelling system implements Decree-Law 2023-17 of 11 March 2023 and the minister's decision of 13 September 2023 setting the procedures and conditions for awarding the labels.

The National Cybersecurity Agency awarded the government cloud (G-Cloud) label to Standard Sharing Software (3S) and EO Data Center in July 2024, after Next Step IT received the first N-Cloud label in April 2024.
